 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice M. R. Mengdey
 Date : 07/02/2025
 Oral Order

1. The present application is filed under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhit, 2023,
for regular bail in connection with FIR being C.R.NO. 11196040230028 of 2023 registered with Cyber Crime Police Station, Vadodara for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 120(B), 114,
419, 354D, 384, 388 and 506 of the IPC and Sections 66(C) and 66(D) of the IT Act.
2.
Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that the in present offence, the investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
The present applicant has been arrested in connection with the present offence on 29.08.2023 and since then the applicant is in custody.
The trial of the offence has not progressed satisfactorily.
He further submitted that the applicant has not committed any offence as alleged in the FIR.

If it was the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23017/2024 ORDER DATED:
07/02/2025 undefined case on the part of the first information that she was being harassed by the present applicant by sending her frequent messages, she could have very well blocked the present applicant to prevent the said harassment.

He, therefore, submitted to allow the present application Rohitkumar Rakeshsing vs State Of Gujarat on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50816788/
1 and enlarge the present applicant on bail subject to suitable conditions.

sentences.text: 3. Learned APP has opposed the present application, inter alia, contending that the offence alleged against the present applicant is of very serious nature.
She, therefore, submitted to dismiss the present application.

4. Learned advocate appearing for the original complainant has also opposed the present application, inter alia, contending that the applicant herein had sent threatening messages to the first informant and had demanded money from her and when the first informant had refused to pay money, she was threatened by the present applicant of dire consequences.
He, therefore, submitted to dismiss the present application.
5. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties and perused the material available on record.
It is the case on the part of prosecution that the present applicant had created a fake profile on matrimonial site and had come into contact with the first informant.

The applicant herein had obtained the obscene photographs of the first informant through coercion from her and on the basis of the said photographs, the applicant herein used to blackmail the first informant and demand money from her.

The first informant had transferred more than Rs.12 lacs in NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23017/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/02/2025 undefined the account instructed by the present applicant and still, the applicant was demanding more money from the first informant and had also threatened her of dire consequence, if she did not pay the amount demanded by the present applicant.

The first informant had also expressed her anguish in one of the messages sent by her to the present applicant, wherein she had said that if the present applicant continued to harass her in said manner, she would commit suicide.
6. So far as the aspect of trial is concerned, the report submitted by the concerned Trial Court indicates that the trial of the offence has commenced.
Having regard to these aspects, no case is made out to release the present applicant on bail.
Hence, the present application stands dismissed.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) GIRISH Rohitkumar Rakeshsing vs State Of Gujarat on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50816788/
